messages.text: Kickoff for ForgeBay, our makerspace checkout helper: members check out consumable materials (filament, plywood, acrylic sheet) and durable tools (calipers, soldering stations). Baseline and standing rules: Python 3.11+, everything fully type-annotated; FastAPI with SQLAlchemy 2.x against a local SQLite file for dev; every new endpoint ships with pytest tests; no new third-party dependencies without asking me first.

Proposed shape: app/ with routers/, models/, schemas/, services/. For out-of-stock holds, I'd suggest Redis with expiring keys instead of sweeping SQL rows — want that? And how should seed data handle member info?

No Redis — no external services at all for now. Holds and every other bit of state live in our application database. Seeds: only fictional member names, ever; never copy real member info out of the office spreadsheet into demo data.
Layout plan, then: models split across catalog.py, checkout.py, members.py; routers mirror them 1:1; Alembic migration 0001 creates members, materials, checkouts. Adopt?
Adopt that layout with one correction — table names are plural snake_case (checkout_items, not CheckoutItem). One more convention: every API error is returned as an RFC 9457 problem+json body.

First chunk of work: build the material catalog — GET /materials listing everything with live stock counts, and POST /checkouts that decrements stock atomically in one transaction. Insufficient stock means refuse with the agreed error format and change nothing. SKU is the public identifier everywhere.

Done: GET /materials, and POST /checkouts doing the stock check plus decrement inside a single transaction, returning a problem+json 409 on insufficient stock with no write. Fully typed; want me to run the suite?
pytest -q: 14 passed, 0 failed. ruff check: no issues. Coverage on routers/catalog.py and routers/checkout.py: 96%.

Nice. Next domain piece: durable tools (calipers, soldering stations) get due dates and an overdue fee — $1 per day late, capped at $10 per checkout. Consumables are never charged fees. Standing convention: all money amounts are stored as integer cents — never floats.
I'll compute overdue from due_date versus now. Cleanest would be a nightly cron that sweeps and posts fees — add an app.scheduled module?

No background daemons or cron in this repo — overdue is computed lazily, at return time and whenever a checkout record is read. Also from ops: staging is approved to run Postgres now, so dev and tests stay on SQLite but keep all queries database-portable — no SQLite-only functions.
Got it — lazy fee computation in the service layer, portable SQL only. One edge case for later: checkouts created before fees existed, do they accrue?

Build it: POST /checkouts/{id}/return for durable tools that computes the overdue fee lazily at return ($1/day, $10 cap, durable tools only, consumables exempt), persists a fee ledger entry, plus GET /fees showing a member's ledger. Leave that legacy edge flagged until I rule on it.

Return flow done: POST /checkouts/{id}/return computes the fee lazily and persists a fee_ledger row; GET /fees lists a member's ledger. The pre-fee-era checkouts are left accruing with a TODO until you decide.
pytest -q: 23 passed, 1 skipped (legacy-fee policy undecided). ruff check: no issues.

Deciding that edge: checkouts created before the fee feature shipped are grandfathered — no fee ever. Separate standing rule: staff-role members may waive any fee, but only with a non-empty reason string, and every waiver must be written to the audit log.

Legacy exemption keyed off created_at; waiver endpoint drafted. Next up: holds on out-of-stock consumables. One question — the front desk has a USB barcode scanner; does checkout need scanner integration?

None — the scanner is just an HID keyboard, it types the SKU and hits enter, so scanner-typed SKUs stay the same optional sku field on checkout. Don't write any driver or SDK code. (When we eventually do the member self-service portal — a different task, not now — we'll want SSO; ignore that for everything current.)

Holds design: material_holds(member_id, material_id, status, ready_at); earliest open hold wins on restock, then a 48-hour pickup window before lapse. Waivers endpoint: POST /fees/{id}/waive, staff-only, reason required. One thing — which timezone anchors the 'day' for due dates and the pickup window?
Store every timestamp in UTC; display in America/Chicago. Due times are end-of-day local — 23:59 America/Chicago on the due date.

Final chunk: implement holds — members place holds on out-of-stock consumables, the earliest open hold wins when stock returns, and the holder gets a 48-hour pickup window before the hold lapses — and finish the staff fee-waiver endpoint per the rules we set. Keep both consistent with all standing conventions.
